statement: This is reminiscent of the arguments justifying the use of the Bethe-Hessian [33]–[35], [72] in graph community detection; we conjecture that an appropriate form of a Bethe-Hessian algorithm can be of use in the hypergraph case. e) Other spectral properties: It remains open to characterize the limiting spectral distribution of B even when q = 2 [22]. When d → ∞ and q = 2, it is known that the real part of the bulk spectral converges to the semicircle law [32], [77]. For Erdős-Rényi graphs with fixed d, an Alon–Boppana-type √ bound was conjectured in [22] that |λ2 (B)| ≥ d + o(1), and we see the same phenomenon from our simulation for Erdős-Rényi hypergraphs. We can also see isolated eigenvalues inside the disk of radius (q − 1)d in our HSBM simulation, which corresponds to the ratio between λ1 (B) and λr (B) for 2 ≤ r ≤ r0 . This “eigenvalue insider” phenomenon for graph SBMs was first observed in [33] when d = O(1), and proved in [32] when d = ω(log n). We conjecture similar results hold for the HSBM.
context: arXiv, the authors in [26] studied spectral clustering algorithms for non-uniform hypergraphs using the non-backtracking operator, and an Ihara-Bass formula for non-uniform hypergraphs was derived. We believe our analysis based on the nonbacktracking operator can be applied to the non-uniform HSBM and reach the threshold conjectured in [26]. d) Possible extensions: The definition of B̃ in (11) and ũi in Theorem 2 imply that for any λ ∈ R, ũi is an eigenvector of the Hermitian matrix Δ(λ) = λ(q − 2 + λ)I − λA + (q − 1)(D − I). This is reminiscent of the arguments justifying the use of the Bethe-Hessian [33]–[35], [72] in graph community detection; we conjecture that an appropriate form of a Bethe-Hessian algorithm can be of use in the hypergraph case. e) Other spectral properties: It remains open to characterize the limiting spectral distribution of B even when q = 2 [22]. When d → ∞ and q = 2, it is known that the real part of the bulk spectral converges to the semicircle law [32], [77]. For Erdős-Rényi graphs with fixed d, an Alon–Boppana-type √ bound was conjectured in [22] that |λ2 (B)| ≥ d + o(1), and we see the same phenomenon from our simulation for Erdős-Rényi hypergraphs. We can also see isolated eigenvalues inside the disk of radius (q − 1)d in our HSBM simulation, which corresponds to the ratio between λ1 (B) and λr (B) for 2 ≤ r ≤ r0 . This “eigenvalue insider” phenomenon for graph SBMs was first observed in [33] when d = O(1), and proved in [32] when d = ω(log n). We conjecture similar results hold for the HSBM. An important special case happens whenever P = αP0 , with P0 constant and α = ω(1) is a scaling parameter. In this case, the RHS of (14) goes to 1 as n → ∞, and hence we can conjecture that Algorithm 2 achieves asymptotically perfect reconstruction. c) Non-uniform hypergraphs: Another natural extension would be to consider models beyond the uniform hypergraph case and allow for different edge sizes. Although the proof of Theorem 1 does not immediately generalize, we believe that our results still hold in the regime where the edge size is upper bounded by a fixed K > 0, and the probability of the presence of a size-q edge scales like cn−(q−1) for any q ≤ K.
